messages.author: f41109c5f2d24e8b
messages.subject: Mesh creation for simulated data
parts:
Hi all,

I am running a simulation study as part of my thesis. I simulated disease cases using spatstat and want to fit an LGCP model (among other methods) to see how well the fixed effects are captured. I tried fitting the model with statspat, but i prefer INLA (inlabru to be specific) for its speed as the number of simulated points increases. 

The problem I have so far is that I cannot seem to create a mesh that doesn't give me unbiased estimates for the non-intercept fixed effects. I believe the issue is the mesh because I've been tinkering with it and have steadily reduced the size of the bias but I can't quite get it there. Since its simulated data, I set the fixed values for the range and sigma because I am not interested in their estimates.

I read the mesh creation section in the "Advanced Spatial Modeling with Stochastic Partial Differential Equations Using R and INLA" textbook as a guide to improve my estimates. I have attached a small snippet of the code for the simulation and subsequent fitting.

Any help is greatly appreciated,

Eke

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Mesh creation for simulated data
parts:
Hi,

for some reason st_as_sf(st_union(cape_town)) set the geometry column name to "x", which the leads fm_int() to, correctly, not interpret "geometry" and "x" as being related to the same space, and your point process model acts on the entire mesh instead of only on the domain of interest.
Either correct it with
  st_geometry(boundary) <- "geometry"
or use a different construction, such as
  st_as_sf(data.frame(geometry=cape_town))

See e.g.
ggplot() +
  gg(facility_dist) +
  geom_fm(data = mesh, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = fm_int(list(geometry = mesh), boundary), aes(size = weight)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size=2)
before and after the above change.

You will still get the "... returned some NA values. ..." warnings for the spatial covariates, but it will fill those in using the closest available value

With that change, I get

Fixed effects:
                 mean    sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant    mode       kld
facility_dist  -2.938 0.351     -3.626   -2.938     -2.249  -2.938    21.202
Intercept     -14.218 0.060    -14.335  -14.218    -14.100 -14.218 14146.754

which matches your simulation values, -3 and -14

One issue you might run into is that modelling in metres may be numerically unstable; transform the data to km units for more stable calculations.
With the development/github version of fmesher, you can do
  crs_km <- fm_crs("EPSF:22234", units = "km")
to construct the needed crs. With the cran version
  crs_km <- fm_crs_set_lengthunit(fm_crs("EPSF:22234"), "km")

You should supply the crs when building the mesh, not override it afterwards, and you should also give it the actual point object, not the raw st_coordinates values, as those drop the crs information.
Do
  fm_mesh_2d(points, ..., crs = crs_km)
instead, as that will build the mesh in crs_km and convert points to that crs if you haven't already done that yourself (with st_transform)

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Mesh creation for simulated data
parts:
When using km length units instead of metres, the point process intensity units changes from m^2 to km^2, i.e. a factor 10^6 smaller, so on the log-scale,
the intercept should become log(10^6) smaller. Multiply the resulting intensity by 10^6 to convert to square metres.

Finn
